name: High Mars Orbit
story: Highly elliptical orbits in the 1,000-2,500 km range, mostly historic. Mariner 9 made it here in 1971 — the first spacecraft to orbit another planet, beating Mars 2 by a few weeks. The Soviet Mars 3 and the American Viking 1 orbiters followed, all parked in long ellipses that minimised station-keeping fuel during the Mariner-era of limited delta-v budgets. Phobos passes through this band at 9,376 km — Viking and Mars Express both used the geometry to study the moon up close.
comparison: Roughly the altitude where Earth's GPS satellites orbit — but around a planet just over half Earth's size. The orbiter's view of Mars at apoapsis is the classic 'whole-disc' framing in early 1970s mission photographs.

firsts.label: Mariner 9 — first artificial satellite of any planet other than Earth (USA)
